# Vault

This repository is a personal knowledge vault: the notes that its owner chose to keep, their projects, and the rules of their assistant, Eva. Eva's code lives in another repository.

Everything stays plain text, so one search finds it and almost any device opens it.

**Eva's identity arrives only as an injected system prompt.** `.eva/assistant.md` holds it, and Eva sends it in Assistant mode. No file loads it by itself. So unless Eva gave you that identity, you are here to work with the notes, not to be Eva.

## What is where

| Path        | What it holds                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Notes/`    | The notes, grouped by topic in subfolders                                                                           |
| `Projects/` | One folder for each project (_Projects_ below)                                                                      |
| `.eva/`     | Eva's files in the vault: `assistant.md` (her rules for this person), `schedules.json`, and her skills in `skills/` |
| `Scratch/`  | Files that are not knowledge: files made to send to a chat, and files received from it. Git ignores it              |

**`.eva/schedules.json` is not a note.** Change it only through the `schedule` skill, because Eva reads it every minute and skips an entry that she cannot read.

**Every path in this file starts at the vault root.**

**No `CLAUDE.md` anywhere in this vault.** Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` only when no `CLAUDE.md` exists in the folder or above it, so one `CLAUDE.md` would hide every `AGENTS.md`.

## Rules

- **One fact lives in one file.** Other files link to it, never copy it.
- **Prefer an update to a new file.** Search first; extend the note that already covers the topic.
- **Name a file after the moment when the person would open it**, not after where its content came from.
- **Secrets** may live only inside the project folder that they belong to. Never copy one anywhere else.
- **Heavy binary files** belong in a cloud drive, not here. A file made only to send goes in `Scratch/`.

## Projects

Each project is a folder `Projects/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm-name/`, named after its creation time. Its `AGENTS.md` starts with YAML front matter:

```yaml
---
created: 2026-01-31T09:15
status: active # idea, active, paused or closed
repos:
  - https://github.com/example/example-app
---
```

Eva clones each repository into `Projects/<id>/repos/<repo>-<n>/`. Git ignores those clones: each one is its own repository.

## Knowledge

### Two ways to group

Notes are grouped along two axes. Pick the axis first, the folder second.

- **By purpose:** general knowledge that outlives any single project. The person wants to find it again later, whatever they work on.
- **By context:** everything about one bounded thing, with mixed purposes together, because the person wants all of it at hand while they work on that thing.

**The test:** does this note still matter after the project or context ends? Yes → purpose. No → context.

So "how we priced the shop" lives in the project. "How I decide prices" moves to `Methods/`.

### Where things go

| Folder           | Why the person opens it                                                                       |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Principles/`    | To remember who they want to be: values, mantras, philosophy.                                 |
| `Methods/`       | To do or decide something their way: their own procedures and frameworks.                     |
| `Toolbox/`       | To grab something and use it: commands, scripts, prompts, cheat sheets, lookup facts.         |
| `Library/`       | To understand something: explanations worth keeping.                                          |
| `Projects/<id>/` | To work on one project: everything about it, any purpose, together.                           |
| `Life/<name>/`   | The same shape, for personal contexts, such as `Life/Home/`, `Life/Health/` or `Life/Diary/`. |

Inside each folder, group by topic. Purpose first, topic second.

**Toolbox or Library?** Ask whether the note gives an action or an understanding. If the person can use it without understanding it, it goes in `Toolbox/`: a command, a script, a prompt. If there is nothing to copy, only something to know, it goes in `Library/`. A mixed note goes where the person opens it from.

### Rules

- **Anything can live in the vault:** notes, documents, scans, photos. Prefer plain text when the content is text. A file made only to send, such as a PDF of an answer, goes in `Scratch/`. Eva also saves there each file that the person sends in the chat, so copy a file worth keeping into the vault.
- **One fact lives in one file.** Other files link to it, never copy it. Two copies drift apart, and then neither can be trusted.
- **Name a file after the moment when the person would open it**, not after where its content came from. Write `Mental Strength Checklist`, not `13 Things Mentally Strong People Don't Do`. The test: standing in that situation, could the person guess the file name?
- **Write notes impersonally**, as statements about the world. Write "The mind believes what it hears by default", not "My mind believes what it hears". A diary is the exception: it is the person's own voice.
- **Write all notes in one language**, so that one search finds everything.
- **Close a note with its source** when the person says where it came from: `> Source: *Title*, Author`, plus a link when one exists.
- **Mark few notes as important.** When the person would want to see a note even while they ask about another topic, put `> Important: <why it matters>` under its title.
- **Secrets** (keys, passwords) may live only inside the project folder that they belong to. Never copy one into a note outside that folder. One known place for each secret makes it possible to change it later.

## Grow the vault

The vault starts empty and grows with each conversation. Keep its shape clear as it grows.

1. **Search first.** Look for notes on the same topic (grep and glob), and compare them with the new information:
   - **Same:** say that it is already stored, name the file, and write nothing.
   - **Conflicting:** show what differs, old against new, and propose to replace the old text.
   - **Incomplete:** add the new information to that note.
   - **Nothing similar:** go on below.
2. **Pick the axis, then the folder,** as _Knowledge_ says.
3. **Create the topic folder** inside that folder when none fits, with a clear name. Never drop a note in the nearest folder because it is close.
4. **Create the note,** and match the names of the files beside it.
5. **Tell the person** where you put it.

Prefer fewer, larger notes. Every extra file makes the important ones harder to find. When a note or a folder grows too long to scan, propose to split it.

**This file is the map of the vault. Keep it true.** When you create, rename or remove a folder at the vault root, change the _What is where_ table in the same commit. A folder that the map does not show gets lost.

**Fix this file yourself when it is simply wrong,** such as a path that moved. **Propose a change and wait when you only prefer it different,** such as a new rule or a new structure. Those carry what the person decided.

2. One of the basics → `Life/About me.md`.
3. Something built remains after the work ends, even when the work has a goal, steps and an end, or a specialist → `Projects/`.

- **Search by name and by alias before you create anything.**
- **When it fits two places,** put it where the person will open it, and link to it from the other. Never copy it.
- **When the meaning is unclear, ask.** Never guess.
- **Nothing moves when it ends.** Close it as its folder's `AGENTS.md` says: a status, a `closed` or `to` day, or its summary.

### Front matter

These rules hold for the front matter of every note, and each `AGENTS.md` in `Life/` adds the keys of its entity.

- **Any note can have these optional keys:**

  - `aliases:` lists other names of the thing, such as `[the car, the blue car]`. A search by name also searches the aliases.

- **Reuse a tag.** Before you add a tag, list the tags that the vault already uses. Pick one that fits. Create a new tag only when none fits.
- **A reference to another note is its path from the vault root,** such as `relation: cousin of Life/People/Marta Example`. In the text, link a note by its path too, so a search for the path finds every note that names it. A thing with no note, such as a company, stays as plain text.

## Projects

Each project is a folder `Projects/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm-name/`, named after the local date and time when it is created, which never change. ```yaml
---
created: 2026-01-31T09:15+01:00 # the folder's date and time, with the offset from UTC
status: active # active, paused or closed
in-use: true # optional: the person uses the project now
closed: # YYYY-MM-DD, when the status becomes closed
objective: The app plans a full week with no manual step. # optional, one line
deadline: { date: 2026-06-15, cost: The demo day passes } # optional
type: software # general, software or specialist. No type means general
summary: A web app that plans the meals of the week. # one line

result: https://example.com/meal-planner # optional: where to use the result
---
```

- **`objective`** says in one line when the project is done. Leave it out for a project that never ends, such as a tool in use. When the objective is reached, propose to close the project, and ask whether the person keeps using it.
- **`deadline`** has the same shape and meaning as in `Life/Cases/AGENTS.md`: a date that someone else set, where missing it costs something. Leave it out when nothing is lost by waiting.
- **`repos`** lists the address of each repository that `git clone` accepts, such as `https://github.com/example/example-app`. - **`## Work and achievements`:** one to three lines for a CV, with no dates. They say what the person built or achieved.
- **`## Links`:** each other address of the project, one per line, with a short label, such as `- Demo video: https://example.com/demo`.

The project types:

- **General:** a folder of notes and files, such as plans, reference photos or drafts: building a house, a scale model, a book. The text under the front matter describes the project.
- **Software:** work in repositories, such as an app. The text under the front matter describes the project and names the repository to read first. Each repository's own `AGENTS.md` holds the rules for its code.
- **Specialist:** a chat with its own rules and memory, such as a gym coach. The text under the front matter holds its rules.

## Rules

### Working in the vault

- **Every path in this file starts at the vault root.**
- **Before you write, search** by name and by alias. If the same fact exists, say where and write nothing. If it conflicts, show old against new and propose the change. If it is incomplete, add to it. Then tell the person where you put it.
- **One fact lives in one file.** Other files link to it, never copy it.
- **Prefer fewer, larger notes.** Propose to split one that grows too long to scan. In a knowledge folder, group by topic, and create a topic folder when none fits.
- **Small files can live in the vault,** beside what they belong to: a contract, a receipt, a scan, a short PDF, a photo of evidence. Anything over about 10 MB goes to the cloud drive, with its link in the note it belongs to.
- **Secrets** live only in encrypted secret files, such as `Wi-Fi.secrets` or `.env.local`. Never copy a secret into a note, a chat or any service, except the person's password manager.

- **Agent files** are this file, each other `AGENTS.md` and each skill in `.eva/skills/`. Fix one yourself when it is simply wrong, such as a path that moved. Propose and wait when you only prefer it different. When the person asks for a change, make it. Never add an `@` import to one.

### Writing

The person can read this prose in a second language. An agent reads it as instructions, so a sentence it can read two ways is a bug.

- **Write all notes in {{notesLanguage}},** even when the person talks in another language. Keep quotes and names in their own language.
- **Prefer plain text,** so one search finds it and any device opens it. Write dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`, and a moment with its offset, as _Front matter_ says.
- **Name a file after the moment when the person opens it,** such as `Mental Strength Checklist`, not after its origin.
